text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) is to hold its annual convention in March, but it is not clear if there will be elections to replace its life-time president Kamuzu Banda, believed to be more than 90 years old.
- Lands and Valuation Minister Peter Fatchi said cabinet has agreed that national consultations be done to seek public opinion on capital punishment.

- Several doctors from Malawi's Queen Elizabeth central hospital, staying at a Blantyre hotel because of a shortage of accommodation, have been kicked out because the hospital has allegedly failed to pay their bills.
